Where Kabul Meets Lahore

Shinwari Fort brings together two great food traditions on one table — the namkeen, fire-first cooking of the Shinwari tribes and the bold, wok-tossed flavours Lahore is famous for.

That means lamb cooked simply and honestly: dumba tikka off the coals, rosh slow-cooked until it falls from the bone, and fragrant Kabuli pulao — alongside Lahori favourites like karahi and makhni handi, made fresh to order.

Find us on Main Boulevard in Gulshan-e-Ravi — bring the family, take your time, and eat the way it has been eaten for generations.

Signature Dishes

The plates Shinwari Fort is known for — from the coals, the handi and the karahi.

From the Coals

Dumba Tikka

Tender lamb, seasoned the Shinwari way and grilled over open flame until the edges char and the centre stays juicy.

Slow-Cooked

Rosh

Lamb simmered low and slow in its own juices with salt and fat — nothing more, nothing less — until it falls apart at a touch.

Afghan Classic

Kabuli Pulao

Fragrant long-grain rice crowned with tender meat, sweet glazed carrots, raisins and slivered almonds.

Hand-Pressed

Chapli Kebab

Flat, hand-pressed minced kebabs with tomato, green chilli and warm spices, fried crisp at the edges.

Rich & Creamy

Makhni Handi

A buttery, cream-rich handi — mild, silky and made for tearing hot naan and sharing around the table.

Lahore Style

Lahori Karahi

Wok-tossed on high heat with fresh tomato, julienned ginger and green chillies — straight from the karahi to your table.

Made for Family Dinners

Shinwari food is sharing food. Platters land in the middle of the table, naan keeps coming, and nobody is in a hurry to leave. Our Gulshan-e-Ravi dining room is set up exactly for that.
